items.longBusinessSummary: Centrus Energy Corp. supplies nuclear fuel components for the nuclear power industry in the United States, Japan, the Netherlands, and internationally. The company operates through two segments: Low-Enriched Uranium (LEU) and Technical Solutions. The LEU segment sells separative work units (SWU) components of LEU; natural uranium hexafluoride, uranium concentrates, and uranium conversion; and enriched uranium products to utilities that operate nuclear power plants. The Technical Solutions segment offers technical, manufacturing, engineering, and operations services to public and private sector customers. The company was formerly known as USEC Inc. and changed its name to Centrus Energy Corp. in September 2014. Centrus Energy Corp. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland.

Item 1.01 Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement
On October 16, 2026 (the “Closing Date”), Centrus Energy Corp. (the “Company”) entered into a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement (the “Purchase Agreement”) with Ventura Trust, not in its individual capacity but solely as trustee of the Westerman Employee Stock Ownership Trust (“Seller”), and Westerman Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Westerman”), pursuant to which on the same date the Company purchased 100% of the issued and outstanding limited liability company membership interests of Westerman (the “LLC Interests”) from the Seller (the “Acquisition”). Westerman is a U.S. equipment manufacturing and engineering firm focused primarily on the energy sector.
As a result of the Acquisition, Westerman is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.
The aggregate purchase price for the LLC Interests was approximately $116.0 million (“Purchase Price”), which was paid by the Company $95.0 million in cash, and $21.0 million in shares (the “Stock Consideration Shares”) of the Company’s Class A common stock, par value $0.10 per share (the “Common Stock”). In connection with Closing, the Company paid, out of the Purchase Price and on behalf of Westerman, an aggregate amount of (a) approximately $31.5 million to the holders of subordinated notes previously issued by Westerman in full satisfaction of the notes and (b) $12.7 million to the lender under a term loan facility of Westerman in full repayment of the loan. In connection with Closing, the Company also paid, out of the Purchase Price, approximately $10.5 million of the Seller’s and Westerman’s transaction expenses. The number of shares of Common Stock issued on the Closing Date was determined based on the closing price of the Common Stock as of October 15, 2026, and were issued pursuant to Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”).
The Purchase Price is subject to a customary cash adjustment based on a final determination of the Closing Net Working Capital (as defined in the Purchase Agreement) as of the Closing Date.
The Company has agreed, as soon as reasonably practicable after the Closing, to use reasonable best efforts to file a registration statement to register the sale of all or a portion of the Stock Consideration Shares on a delayed or continuous basis in accordance with Rule 415 of the Securities Act, which shall be an “automatic shelf registration statement” as defined in Rule 405 (or successor rule) promulgated under the Securities Act.
The Purchase Agreement includes representations, warranties and covenants of the parties customary for a transaction of this nature. The representations and warranties contained in the Purchase Agreement did not survive the closing of the transaction (“Closing”), and the parties have waived all post-Closing claims against each other related to the representations and warranties, except in the case of fraud. At Closing, the Company obtained a buyer-side representations and warranties insurance policy. Further, the Company delivered at the Closing executed retention agreements with certain key employees.
The foregoing description of the Purchase Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the Purchase Agreement, which is filed as Exhibit 2.1 hereto and which is incorporated herein by reference. The Purchase Agreement has been filed to provide information to investors regarding its terms. It is not intended to provide any other factual information about the parties to the Purchase Agreement. The representations, warranties and covenants contained in the Purchase Agreement were made only for purposes of the Purchase Agreement and as of specific dates, were solely for the benefit of the parties thereto, may be subject to limitations agreed upon by the contracting parties, and may be subject to standards of materiality that differ from those applicable to investors. Investors are not third-party beneficiaries under the Purchase Agreement and should not rely on the representations, warranties and covenants or any descriptions thereof as characterizations of the actual state of facts or condition of the Company, Westerman or any of their respective subsidiaries or affiliates.

Item 7.01 Regulation FD Disclosure.
On October 19, 2026, the Company issued a press release announcing the entry into the Purchase Agreement and the completion of the transactions contemplated thereby. A copy of the press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated herein by reference.
The information in this Item 7.01 and Exhibit 99.1 is being furnished pursuant to Item 7.01 of Form 8-K and shall not be deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, or otherwise subject to the liabilities of that section, nor shall it be deemed incorporated by reference in any filing under the Securities Act of 1933 or the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 except as may be expressly set forth by specific reference in such filing.

Title: Centrus Energy Acquires Westerman Holdings for $116 Million to Expand Manufacturing Capacity
Author: Fiona Craig   Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:56 PM GMT+2 5 min read
Published: 2026-10-19T12:56:08+00:00
=== BODY ===
Centrus Energy Corp. (NYSE:LEU) announced the acquisition of Westerman Holdings for approximately $116 million, as the nuclear fuel supplier seeks to expand its manufacturing capabilities and secure components required for its uranium enrichment operations.
The transaction was financed through approximately $95 million in cash and $21 million in equity.
Centrus shares advanced following the announcement, although the company did not provide a specific percentage movement in the information released.
The acquisition brings an existing supplier of centrifuge components under Centrus's ownership and adds manufacturing operations serving the nuclear, oil and gas, and broader industrial sectors.
Centrus expects the transaction to contribute positively to adjusted earnings per share during the first year following completion.
Westerman Holdings currently manufactures centrifuge casings and other major components used in Centrus's uranium enrichment operations.
By acquiring the company, Centrus intends to integrate a portion of its manufacturing supply chain and increase control over the production of equipment required for its planned capacity expansion.
Centrifuges are used in uranium enrichment to separate uranium isotopes, a process that produces fuel suitable for use in commercial nuclear reactors.
Manufacturing the specialised components required for these systems is an important part of developing and maintaining enrichment capacity.
Centrus said the acquisition would support its ability to obtain these components as it expands production.
The company also expects the integration to reduce certain project costs and improve operational efficiency.
However, it did not disclose specific cost-saving targets or a timetable for achieving the anticipated efficiencies.
The acquisition forms part of Centrus's previously announced multibillion-dollar programme to expand uranium enrichment capacity.
The company is investing in manufacturing and production capabilities intended to support the development of additional enrichment infrastructure.
Westerman's existing relationship with Centrus means the acquired business already produces components used in the company's centrifuge systems.
Bringing these activities under common ownership is intended to provide greater coordination between equipment manufacturing and enrichment capacity development.
Centrus expects the transaction to improve supply chain integration as it progresses with its expansion plans.
The company has not provided revised capital expenditure forecasts or updated enrichment capacity targets specifically associated with the acquisition.
Centrus anticipates that the acquisition will be accretive to adjusted earnings per share during the first year following closing.
An accretive acquisition is one that is expected to increase the acquiring company's earnings per share relative to its performance without the transaction.
The anticipated contribution will depend on Westerman's financial performance, integration costs and the operational benefits achieved following the acquisition.
Centrus also expects to reduce project costs through closer coordination of manufacturing and procurement activities.
The company did not disclose Westerman's annual revenue, adjusted EBITDA or net income in the announcement.
As a result, the acquisition's expected financial contribution cannot be independently quantified from the information provided.
Founded in 1909, Westerman operates four manufacturing facilities across Ohio, Oklahoma and Wyoming.
The company employs approximately 400 people and produces equipment for customers in several industrial markets.
Its operations include manufacturing products for upstream and midstream oil and gas activities, engineered industrial systems and specialised nuclear applications.
Westerman also produces nuclear-grade equipment, including uranium hexafluoride (UF6) cylinders.
UF6 cylinders are used for the handling, storage and transportation of uranium hexafluoride, a material associated with uranium conversion and enrichment processes.
The acquisition therefore expands Centrus's manufacturing activities beyond components used exclusively in its own enrichment operations.
Westerman's existing industrial customer relationships will also become part of the enlarged group's business.
Amir Vexler, President and Chief Executive Officer of Centrus Energy, said the acquisition would support the company's manufacturing expansion and broaden its customer base.
"Bringing Westerman in-house demonstrates our commitment to securing our supply chain to support our build-out while adding to our capabilities and expanding our customer base," Vexler said.
The transaction is intended to address both the availability of centrifuge components and the development of additional industrial manufacturing capabilities.
Centrus expects the combination to provide operational benefits as it advances its enrichment capacity programme.
The extent of those benefits will depend on the integration of Westerman's operations and the execution of the company's expansion plans.
Following the acquisition, Westerman will continue operating under its existing name as a subsidiary of Centrus Energy.
The company has also announced changes to Westerman's management structure.
Jacob Garrett, currently Chief Executive Officer of Westerman, will become President of Westerman and take on the additional role of Vice President of Centrus Energy.
The arrangement is intended to maintain operational continuity while incorporating Westerman into Centrus's wider business.
Centrus did not announce plans to close facilities or reduce Westerman's workforce as part of the transaction.
The company also did not disclose additional organisational changes beyond the management appointments.
The approximately $116 million acquisition consideration consists of two components: around $95 million in cash and $21 million in equity.
The cash component represents approximately 82% of the total consideration, with equity accounting for the remaining 18%.
Centrus did not provide further details about the equity instruments issued or the effect of the transaction on its capital structure.
Barclays acted as financial adviser to Centrus.
Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz served as legal counsel for the transaction.
The announcement did not include additional information about transaction-related expenses or financing arrangements beyond the disclosed consideration.
Centrus Energy's acquisition of Westerman Holdings adds an established industrial manufacturer and existing centrifuge component supplier to the company's operations.
The transaction supports Centrus's multibillion-dollar uranium enrichment expansion programme while introducing additional manufacturing activities serving non-nuclear customers.
Management expects the acquisition to contribute to adjusted earnings per share during the first year and generate operational efficiencies through greater supply chain integration.
Investors will be monitoring Westerman's contribution to Centrus's financial results, progress on enrichment capacity expansion and any subsequent disclosures about integration costs and expected savings.
The acquisition's longer-term financial impact will depend on manufacturing demand, operational performance and the execution of Centrus's investment programme.
